1 (By Sri N Nagaraju, Advocate)
 JUDGMENT
This claim petition is filed by the petitioner under Section 166 of Indian Motor Vehicles Act, seeking compensation for the injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident.

2. The case of the petitioner is as follows:-
That on 16-01-2025 at about 6-30 to 06-35 pm., the petitioner as pedestrian was walking on Bangalore - Kanakapura road and when he reached Nettigere gate,
Kanakapura - Bengaluru road, Uttrahalli Hobali, Bengaluru, at that time the rider of Yamaha motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KL-59-T-5372 came from Kanakapura side towards Bengaluru side in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the petitioner from behind, result of which the petitioner sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately, the petitioner was shifted to Sanjaygandhi Hospital, Bengaluru wherein first aid treatment was given and then he was shifted to KIMS Hospital and after further management shifted to Leelavathi Hospital, Bengaluru wherein admitted as an inpatient from 16-01-2015 to 20-01-2025.
So far, the petitioner has spent sum of Rs.5,00,000/- towards medical expenses and other incidental charges.
3. Prior to the accident, the petitioner was hale and healthy.
He was aged about 55 years.
He was doing milk vending work and earning sum of Rs.30,000/- per month.

Due to the accidental injuries,
the petitioner has suffered pain and sufferings, permanent disability, loss of future income and other pecuniary and non-pecuniary damages.

4. The Respondent no.1 /owner of Yamaha motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KL-59-T-5372 has filed written statement and admitted that he is the owner of the said motorcycle and same was insured with the respondent no.1.
The respondent no.1 has contended that the alleged accident has occurred due to the negligent act on the part of the petitioner 5.

The Respondent no.2 /insurer of Yamaha motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KL-59-T-5372 has filed written statement and admitted the coverage of insurance policy and the liability if any subject to the terms and conditions mentioned in the policy.

The respondent no.2 has contended that their insured vehicle was not at all involved in the accident and the said vehicle has been falsely implicated by the petitioner with active collusion of the owner of the motorcycle and police, in order to get compensation and that there is two days delay in lodging the complaint and that the rider of the said motorcycle was not holding valid and effective driving license.
6. On the basis of the above pleadings the following issues are framed:
ISSUES Jayanna vs Navin Wilson on 3 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/147269301/
2 1.

Whether the Petitioner proves that he has sustained injuries on account of road traffic accident on 16-01-2025 at about 6-30 to 06-35 pm., at Nettigere gate,
Bengaluru - Kanakapura road, Uttrahalli Hobali, Bengaluru South, Bangalore, due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of Yamaha motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KL-59-T-5372?
2. Whether petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so, what is the quantum?

from whom?
3.
What order or award?
7. The petitioner got examined himself as Pw1 and one witness as P.W.2 and got marked documents at Ex.P1 to Ex.P13 and closed his evidence.
The respondents have not adduced any evidence on their behalf.

8. Heard arguments of learned counsel for petitioner and respondents and perused the entire materials placed on record.
9.

My findings on the above issues are as follows:
 Issue No.1: In the Affirmative  Issue No.2: Partly in the affirmative.
Issue No.3:

As per final order,
 for the following;

REASONS 10. Issue No.1:- In order to explain the actionable negligence of the driver of offending vehicle, the P.W.1 has filed his affidavit explaining the vivid picture of the accident that took place on 16-01-2025 at about 6-30 to 06-35 pm., when the petitioner as pedestrian was walking on Bangalore -Kanakapura road and when he reached Nettigere gate, Kanakapura - Bengaluru road, Uttrahalli Hobali, Bengaluru

, at that time Yamaha motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KL-59-T-5372 (hereinafter referred as the offending vehicle) came from Kanakapura side towards Bengaluru side in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the petitioner from behind, result of which he sustained grievous injuries.

P.W.1 further deposed about the nature of injuries sustained, treatment taken and the amount spent for treatment etc.
11.

In support of the claim and to prove the rash and negligent driving, the P.W.1 has relied upon Ex.P1 to 6 which are the police records such as F.I.R with complaint, Spot mahazar, IMV report,
wound certificate, charge sheet, notice u/Sec. 133 of IMV Act and reply given thereon etc.,
12.

On the basis of the complaint lodged by Arun Kumar J, case has been registered against the rider of offending vehicle in Crime No.0014/2025 by Kaggalipura Police Station for the offence punishable under section 125(a), 281 of BNS 2023.

After completion of investigation, the Jayanna vs Navin Wilson on 3 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/147269301/
3 investigating officer has filed charge sheet against the rider of offending vehicle for the offence punishable under Section under section 125(a), 281 of BNS 2023.
13.

sentences.text: The learned counsel for respondent no.2 during the course of argument has disputed the manner of accident one stated by the petitioner and submitted that the accident in question has occurred while petitioner was crossing the road hence the petitioner too has contributed negligence.

14. Per contra, the petitioner has contended that the accident in question has occurred while he was walking on the extreme left side of Bangalore - Kanakapura road at Nettigere gate and offending vehicle which came from Kanakapura side in rash and negligent manner hit against him.

15. In the light of the rival contention taken by the parties, if the complaint, FIR and charge sheet is perused, wherein it is clearly stated that the accident in question has occurred when the petitioner was crossing the road.
If the spot mahazar and sketch is perused, the width of the road at the spot of accident is nearly 40 feet.
The spot of accident is at a distance of nearly 5 feet from the left edge of tar road towards right side.

The PW.1 in his evidence has deposed that after crossing Bangalore- Kanakapura road, when he was waiting for bus on the left side of Kanakapura - Bangalore road to go to K G Gollarapalya at that time the offending vehicle came in a rash and negligent manner hit against him.
But the spot mahazar and sketch negatives the contention taken by the petitioner.
If petitioner was waiting for bus in the bus stand there was no necessity for him to present at the spot which is a tar road that too National High way.
Hence, the police records clearly discloses that the petitioner while crossing the road met with an accident.

The petitioner being a pedestrian while crossing the road more particularly in the National High way ought to have been more careful because much vehicles are plying in the National High way at a high speed.
Hence, it can be said that the petitioner too has contributed negligence.
Further when the width of the road is nearly 40 feet and when it is a straight road and it is one way road and nearly 35 feet road was left on the right side of the spot of accident.

Under such circumstances, if the driver of the offending vehicle drove his vehicle in moderate speed with all caution, on seeing the petitioner crossing the road, he could have avoided the accident by applying break and he could have taken his vehicle on the right side of the road.
Hence, it can be said that the driver of the offending vehicle has contributed higher amount of negligence.
Hence, the negligence contributed by the petitioner is assessed at 10% and the driver of the offending vehicle at 90%.
Hence, the petitioner has to forgo compensation to an extent of 10% of negligence contributed by him.
Accordingly issue no.1 is answered in partly affirmative.
16. Issue No.2:-
The petitioner has given evidence to the effect of his sustained grievous injuries.
As observed earlier, petitioner has produced medical documents i.e., Wound certificate and Discharge summary which are marked at Ex.P4 and P7.

On going through the medical documents it reveal that petitioner has taken treatment as inpatient at Leelavathi Multi Speciality Hospital, Bangalore from 16-01-2025 to 20- 01-2025 for a period of 4 days and again admitted as an inpatient from 02-04-2025 to 04-04-2025 and thus he has taken treatment as an inpatient for nearly 6 days.
As per wound certificate the petitioner has sustained two injuries of which injury no.1 is simple in nature and injury no.2 is grievous in nature.

4 17.
Dr. Nagaraj B N - Orthopedic surgeon at Sai Ortho And Dental Senter, Bangalore is examined as Pw-2 and through him Clinical notes and x-ray are got marked as Ex.P12 and Ex.P13.

sentences.text: The PW.2 has deposed that he examined the petitioner on 15-07-2025 clinically, radiologically for assessment of disability.

PW.2 further deposed that petitioner has suffered permanent physical disability of left lower limb at 76% and to the whole body at 25% and the petitioner requires Rs.60,000/- for removal of implant.
18.

In the cross examination it is admitted by Pw.2 that he has not given treatment to the petitioner and that since there was infection in the surgical site, implant was removed and external fixation was done and on 02-04- 2025 to 04-04-2025, the petitioner got admitted for infective non union of left tibia.

According to the PW.2 fracture is not united and petitioner is taking follow up treatment and that since fracture is not united and external fixation is yet to be removed, he has assessed the disability at premature stage and that after the fracture is united, there may be variation in the percentage of disability suffered by the petitioner.
19. From the evidence of PW.2 it can be gathered that he has assessed the disability at premature stage.
Hence, this court instead of considering the disability of 25% assessed by the PW.2 on whole body would consider the disability at 15%.
20. Hence, considering the nature of injuries sustained, period of treatment taken this court is of the opinion that petitioner is entitled for compensation under different heads.
21. Towards pain and sufferings, petitioner shown to have sustained one grievous injury.

Hence taking into consideration the nature of injury sustained by the petitioner and time taken for treatment and sufferings during the treatment it is reasonable to hold that petitioner is entitled for sum of Rs.70,000/- towards pain and suffering.
22. So far as the medical expenses incurred by the petitioner is concerned, he has produced 17 medical bills for Rs.2,31,369/- as per Ex.P8.
As such petitioner is entitled for Rs.2,31,369/- under the head medical expenses.
23. It is stated that petitioner was doing agricultural works at K G Gollarapalya village and was earning more than Rs.30,000/- per month.
But, he has not produced any document to prove his income and avocation.

Hence this court considering the age of the petitioner, the year of accident and place of residence considers the income of the petitioner as Rs.17,000/- p.m.
24.
The petitioner has sustained one grievous injury and taken treatment for 6 days as an inpatient in Leelavathi Multi Speciality Hospital, Bangalore.
Hence, it is reasonable to hold that period of three months as complete laid down period.

Hence taking into consideration the avocation of the petitioner and loss of income caused from the said avocation this Tribunal takes the loss of income during laid down period as Rs.17,000/- p.m for three months.
Hence petitioner is entitled for sum of Rs.51,000/- towards loss of income during the laid down period.

5 25.
From the evidence of Pw.1 and as borne out by medical records, petitioner has taken treatment at Leelavathi Multi Speciality Hospital, Bangalore.
For 06 days of hospitalization requires an attendant, was traveled to hospital for treatment.
He has taken nourishment and need further nourishment at this age and incurred other incidental expenses.

Therefore all together incidental expenses is assessed at Rs.25,000/-
taking in to consideration the cost of living and value of the money during the year 2025.
26.
It is stated by the petitioner that at the time of accident he was aged about 55 years.
In this regard, he has produced his Aadhaar card/Ex.P11 which shows his date of birth as 01-01-1968.
As the accident took place in the year 2025, the petitioner was aged about 57 years.

The learned counsel for respondent no.2 by referring the evidence of PW.1 wherein he has stated that the age of his daughter may be 40 years has argued that when the age of the daughter of petitioner is 40 years,
there is no reason to believe that the petitioner was aged 55 years as on the date of accident, but he is aged more than 65 years.

But when petitioner has produced Aadhar card and petitioner on assumption has stated that the age of his daughter is 40 years, on that ground alone, it cannot be said that petitioner was aged more than 65 years as on the date of accident.
Hence, the age of the petitioner is considered as 57 years.

27. So taking into consideration the monthly income of the petitioner having considered by this tribunal as Rs.17,000/- p.m, if 15% of loss of earning capacity is considered and when the age of the petitioner at the time of accident was 57 years, as per Sarla Varma's case the multiplier applicable to the age group of 56 to 60 is '9".
So by applying the multiplier '9' the future loss of income due to disability comes to Rs.2,75,400/- (i.e., 17,000 x 15% x 9 x12).
Hence this Tribunal holds that the petitioner is entitled for Rs.2,75,400/- towards future loss of income due to disability.
28. So far as future medical expense is concerned, even though PW.2 has deposed that the petitioner needs surgery in the form of implant removal and it would cost around Rs.60,000/-.
But he has not given any estimation

Hence, this court awards compensation under the head future medical expenses to the tune of Rs.30,000/-.
29.
The petitioner at his age of 57 years has suffered grievous injury.
Hence taking in to consideration the said aspect the petitioner is entitled for sum of Rs.50,000/- towards loss of amenities and discomforts.

Thereby petitioner is entitled to the compensation as under:
Sl. Under the Heads Amount No. (in Rupees )
 1. Towards pain and sufferings Rs. 70,000/-
 2. Medical expenses Rs. 2,31,369/-
 3. Towards loss of income during Rs. 51,000/-
 laid up period  4. Towards Conveyance, Attendant Rs. 25,000/-
 charges and nourishing food Jayanna vs Navin Wilson on 3 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/147269301/
6  5. Future Loss of Income Rs. 2,75,400/-
 6

Future medical expenses 30,000/-
 7. Loss of amenities and discomfort Rs. 50,000/-
Total Rs. Rs.7,32,769/-

Therefore this court holds that petitioner is entitled for Rs.7,32,769/- (Rupees Seven Lakh Thirty Two Thousand Seven Hundred Sixty Nine only).
30.
As regarding liability is concerned, there is no dispute that offending vehicle was insured with 2nd respondent and policy was in force as on the date of accident.
Further the rider of offending vehicle had driving license to drive the offending vehicle.
Hence it can be said that all the documents pertaining to the vehicle in question was valid and in force as on the date of accident.

Since both petitioner and respondent no.2 had contributed negligence to the extent of 10:90 this court has already come to the conclusion that out of the total compensation amount, petitioner has to forgo compensation to an extent of 10%.
The respondent no 2 being the insurer is liable to pay 90% of the awarded compensation to the petitioners.
90% of the compensation shall carry interest at the rate of 6% p.a.
accordingly issue no 2 is answered.
31. Issue No.3:
In the light of the findings given on Issue No.1 and 2, my finding on this issue is as per the following final order.
ORDER The claim petition filed by the petitioner is hereby allowed in part with costs.

The petitioner is entitled to a total compensation of Rs.7,32,769/- (Rupees Seven Lakh Thirty Two Thousand Seven Hundred Sixty Nine only).
The Respondent No 2 is liable to pay 90% of the compensation amount i.e., sum of Rs.6,59,492/- +
cost of Rs.300/- imposed vide order on IA No. II, in all sum of Rs.6,59,792/- (Rupees Six Lakh Fifty Nine Thousand Seven Hundred Ninety Two only) with interest on sum of Rs.6,29,492/- at 6% pa.,
within 2 months from the date of this award.
It shall also carry interest at 6% per annum on Rs.6,29,492/- from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
Petitioner shall forgo 10% of the compensation amount i.e., to the extent of Rs.73,277/-.

On deposit of the said amount and interest, 50% of compensation payable to the petitioner shall be deposited in his name in any nationalized bank of the choice of petitioner for a period of 3 years and the remaining 50% shall be released to the petitioner through E-payment on proper identification.
Advocates' fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
(Dictated to the stenographer directly on computer, corrected and then pronounced by me in open court, on this the 3rd day of September 2025.)
(ROOPASHRI) XXII Addl. SCJ & ACJM Bengaluru.
